feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader with clear domain focus, solid progression, and relevant platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a strong niche in public-sector digital platforms, governance, and communications systems.  
- Credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with steady advancement from coordinator to director signals trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good evidence of scale: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” strengthen impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: skills and tools appear across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; consolidate to create more space for achievements and outcomes.  
- Add more quantified results: several bullets describe responsibilities well but would be stronger with measurable outcomes (engagement growth, efficiency gains, campaign performance, cost savings).  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists varies (“social, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and video”); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce abstraction: replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add a concrete scale marker from recent work, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Prioritize the most relevant leadership themes: enterprise web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, and AI-enabled search; multimedia can be secondary.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Built and scaled digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, and editorial systems supporting complex, mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration and AI-enabled search experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search.”
- “Multimedia production” is already well covered elsewhere; avoid overemphasizing it in the intro unless targeting communications-heavy roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Prioritize the most senior/recent strengths and reduce generic items like “Multi-channel communications operations.”
- Consider this tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboarding, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and structured content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows, add one more differentiator tied to scope, e.g., “Cross-channel content operations” or “Drupal-based platform leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats the header and recent projects almost verbatim.
- Several items duplicate Topline Skills categories; this section should stay higher-level, not mirror them.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in recent NACo roles. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more additive and less like a second summary.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and trim stacked nouns: e.g., “Created an AI-powered legislative search tool using hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level chat.”
- Where possible, add scale or purpose consistently: audience, campaign use, conference setting, or organizational impact.
- Standardize style: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for cleaner CV style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current consultant and NACo experience bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider emphasizing similarly unique projects or outcomes here.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the earlier NACo staff roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + level: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and communications operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-led bullets; e.g. “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits to support advocacy and engagement initiatives.”
- Rephrase technical work to show business value: “Improved content workflows, analytics, and cross-channel governance across web, email, social, and multimedia to strengthen coordinated communications.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains, or stakeholder adoption of AI search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital strategy, content operations, enterprise web improvement” overlaps heavily with the 2022–2024 Director role; emphasize consultant/advisory capacity and new initiatives.
- AI search and microsite work already appear in Recent Projects, so keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and audience growth.”
- Rewrite the website bullet to foreground transformation: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel/video bullets more results-focused: add engagement, production volume, cost savings, turnaround time, or in-house capacity metrics if available.
- Combine analytics/governance into one concise operations bullet: “Built reporting infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, while formalizing governance, publishing standards and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and outcome-focused.
- Video/programming language partially repeats older NACo roles; emphasize the studio build and organizational capability shift here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your leadership at this level, and tighten phrasing around outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy content delivery.”
- Tighten bullets to focus on distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet for impact: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger outcome-oriented line: “Built more structured editorial planning and cross-team publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and execution speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is too close to the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” instead.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this here as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

- Editorial systems and governance

- Audience-focused content planning

Suggested edit:

- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for high-volume publishing
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy

Suggested edit:

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and currently duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize platform administration strength or differentiated by adding level/scope.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise CMS) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add light qualifiers tied to recent work: Drupal (10,000+ page migration; enterprise publishing) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Standardize naming for professionalism: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages.”
- Consider ordering by relevance/recency: Drupal first, then WordPress/SharePoint, with GitHub Pages last as the least central.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical depth.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor compared with the enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it sharper by emphasizing implementation level and grouping tools by function.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS/JavaScript (front-end implementation) • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value and date the section.
- Consider adding scope/level if accurate: “front-end implementation,” “light scripting,” or “deployment automation” to clarify hands-on capability.
- If you have concrete recent use, replace one tool with a stronger outcome-linked term, e.g., “serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers)” or “CI/CD automation (GitHub Actions).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- If GTM is used mainly for analytics, it may fit better under Analytics/Optimization rather than Coding & Technical Implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow/systems” claims elsewhere. Make it more selective and role-relevant by emphasizing automation/build tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Project Systems**
- Prioritize higher-signal tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- Move lower-value collaboration tools to a separate item only if space allows: **Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Drop older/generic project tools unless specifically used recently or deeply: **Basecamp • Trello**

Suggested edit:
- **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**  
  Optional expanded version: **Airtable systems • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are collaboration platforms, not strong differentiators for a senior digital strategy profile.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare software list and misses the scale/strategic email work shown in recent NACo roles. Strengthen it by signaling CRM/email automation capability without repeating newsletter details already covered in experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Email campaign operations • Audience segmentation • Journey automation**
- If you have evidence, replace generic terms with stronger specifics: **list management**, **template deployment**, **A/B testing**, **performance reporting**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest platform first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like “tens of thousands of recipients” here; that’s already covered well in Work Experience
- “Engagement Systems” overlaps slightly with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; use CRM/email-specific wording to keep the distinction clear

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and reads as a generic keyword dump. Keep it tighter and more execution-focused so it supports recent analytics leadership without repeating the same exact terms elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Tighten content to: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- Use more precise phrasing: replace broad **SEO** with **SEO analysis** and **Dashboarding** with **KPI dashboarding** to signal business application.
- If space allows elsewhere, move outcomes to recent NACo roles instead of here, e.g., analytics stack expansion supporting reporting for a 10,000+ page site and 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping tools here and moving concepts like KPI design/performance analysis to Topline Skills only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role; avoid repeating all of them verbatim in multiple sections if space is tight.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more concrete, emphasize “firsts” and team-building, and trim duties that are repeated in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows spanning web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add specific outputs or scale if available: website size/traffic at refresh, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten the second sentence to focus on distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and supervised a digital media associate.”
- Replace soft phrasing like “high-impact” and “day-to-day guidance” with measurable or stronger verbs: launched, produced, streamlined, supervised, trained.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep it here only if this role launched the series.
- Workflow/editorial coordination language also appears in later NACo entries; keep this version focused on building the initial team and systems.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia work, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete research/program support outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to foreground the most distinctive achievement: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research, program coordination, and digital content production; launched NACo’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “coordinated innovation and research projects” with specifics if possible: topic areas, number of projects, audiences served, or deliverables produced.
- Add measurable scope where available: number of episodes, stakeholders/interviewees, multimedia assets, or programs supported.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles since those carry more strategic weight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with the 2015–2018 Digital Media Manager/Producer role; keep this item focused on podcast launch and research/program coordination.
- Avoid repeating generic web/email/social language already covered more strongly in 2018–2024 entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. In a senior CV, this section should stay tool-focused and avoid repeating broader capabilities already proven in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename or tighten to emphasize software/tools only:  
  **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator**
